unresolved_added: The printed CDF derivation retains squared terms and dy_C in its alleged antiderivative. Preserve the source form as evidence only and re-derive the integral before numeric reuse.
The translated impact variable Y_I=Y_C+Gh should shift both support limits, but the printed upper support remains y_B-y_R rather than y_B-y_R+Gh.
The joint density inherits the impact-density support inconsistency, so its normalization and every downstream regional integral require a corrected support audit.
The printed indexed x inequality is not an unambiguous lower-and-upper cell-bound contract; the role and sign of l must be made explicit before generating corners.
The printed y bound uses y_B-y_0-Gh and does not clearly preserve the earlier radar-horizon and impact-support terms, creating a geometry mismatch between density, partition, and coordinates.
rho is described as miles per degree but is multiplied in C_L=rho R C+y_0. A miles-to-degrees transform normally requires the reciprocal convention, so units and direction must be reconciled.

Multiplying the searched-cell POC by 1-POD is a likelihood step, but the subsequent uniform mass redistribution is a mass-conserving heuristic rather than a normalized Bayesian posterior conditioned on nondetection.
Selecting the largest updated adjacent POC reduces some travel relative to unrestricted probability chasing, but no global time, fuel, coverage, or detection-optimality proof is supplied.
Separate one-at-a-time curves for G and theta do not establish the prose claim about the combined quantity G+theta; joint interactions and parameter domains are not tested.
The altitude discussion refers to Figure 4 while the relevant plot is Figure 7, so figure-to-claim traceability is broken at the point of sensitivity interpretation.

The prose says POD increases with search altitude, but the plotted curve and square-root detector term decrease as altitude approaches effective instrument reach; the later low-altitude recommendation contradicts the first sentence.
Figure 8 varies search-plane count n but its caption labels the curve POD(h_s), so the displayed independent variable must be recovered from axes and surrounding prose.
Flight ABCD's numerical impact-density center and support do not transparently follow the general Y_I=Y_C+Gh translation, and no normalization or substitution audit is shown.
The methodology defines the condition factor as kappa, but the worked-example and Appendix C POD expression use k; the executable code must bind one symbol explicitly.
Appendix A integrates y_I from zero-based partition bounds and does not visibly add the Gh offset used by the impact variable, so its 36 POC values may not represent the declared density support.
Appendices C and D apply Ceiling to a probability-matrix redistribution term. Integer rounding is incompatible with fractional POC conservation and may collapse or inflate the update.

The Mathematica While conditions are separated by semicolons, and local 3x3 minima are matched through a global Position call. Loop termination, index safety, and selected-cell locality are not executable without clarification.

Appendix C is introduced as the neighborhood algorithm in the body but its page-28 heading says the loop is without adjacency, conflicting with the local 3x3 selection intended to distinguish it from Appendix D.
The conclusion claims applicability to all aircraft and search-plane types from one hypothetical Boeing 777 scenario with uncalibrated sensing and no field comparator.

Claims that the plan is valid, maximizes resources, is a breakthrough, and will be implemented are not supported by optimization certificates, calibrated data, field validation, or deployment evidence.
